title: anndata.claude
text: AnnData: annotated data matrix n_obs observations n_vars variables, aligned annotations unstructured metadata. Avoid: SingleCellExperiment, Seurat object, dataset Observation: row AnnData, usually cell. Avoid: sample, column Variable: column AnnData, usually gene feature. Avoid: feature, row Slot: One named component AnnData: X, obs, var, obsm, varm, obsp, varp, layers, uns raw. Avoid: field, attribute, assay obs_names / var_names: string identifiers observations variables, may contain duplicates. Avoid: rownames, colnames, barcodes Aligned mapping: slot holding named elements whose dimensions must match n_obs /n_vars (obsm, varm, obsp, varp, layers). uns: slot holding unstructured metadata nested mapping arbitrary encodable values. View: AnnData produced subsetting shares data parent modified, becomes independent copy. Avoid: slice, subset object raw: frozen copy X, var varm kept variable filtering, sharing observations parent.

title: anndata.claude
text: Element: single stored value file (array, sparse matrix, dataframe, mapping scalar) identified path. Encoding type: encoding-type attribute naming Element stored, csr_matrix, dataframe categorical. Encoding version: encoding-version attribute giving version Encoding type’s layout. -disk dtype: exact storage type Element’s data (e.g. float32, int64, uint8), R may represent natively. Round trip: Reading file writing back (R R, Python R Python R Python R) every Element keeps Encoding type, Encoding version, -disk dtype values, object read equal whichever language read wrote . Avoid: conversion, export Structural equivalence: Two Stores (different formats) tree groups arrays, attributes, Encoding types versions, -disk dtypes, shapes values, regardless byte layout. Avoid: identical files Store: file directory holding AnnData disk: h5ad file zarr store (v2 v3). Avoid: container Shard: zarr v3 file holding many chunks one array index, written default Python (auto_shard_zarr_v3). Shard chunk layout part Structural equivalence. title: Getting started with anndata.claude
text: AnnData holds matrix X observations (obs) rows variables (var) columns.
code: X <- matrix(as.numeric(1:12), nrow = 3) obs <- data.frame(   cell_type = c("T", "B", "T"),   row.names = c("cell1", "cell2", "cell3") ) var <- data.frame(   highly_variable = c(TRUE, FALSE, TRUE, FALSE),   row.names = c("gene1", "gene2", "gene3", "gene4") ) adata <- AnnData(X, obs = obs, var = var) adata #> AnnData object with n_obs × n_vars = 3 × 4 #>     obs: 'cell_type' #>     var: 'highly_variable' #>     layers: None (.X)

title: Getting started with anndata.claude
text: Annotations aligned obs var kept obsm, varm, obsp, varp layers. Unstructured data goes uns.
code: adata$obsm[["pca"]] <- matrix(c(0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 1, 2, 3), nrow = 3) adata$layers[["counts"]] <- X * 2 adata$uns[["note"]] <- "example" adata$obs[["batch"]] <- c("a", "a", "b") adata #> AnnData object with n_obs × n_vars = 3 × 4 #>     obs: 'cell_type', 'batch' #>     var: 'highly_variable' #>     uns: 'note' #>     obsm: 'pca' #>     layers: 'counts', None (.X)

Values extracted View plain R objects, unlike Python x <- sub$X; x[1, 1] <- 0 change View. Assign View (sub$X[1, 1] <- 0) instead. differences Python listed vignette("deviations").

title: Getting started with anndata.claude
text: Use compression = "gzip" compress datasets, as_sparse read_h5ad() read dense X sparse matrix.
code: path <- tempfile(fileext = ".h5ad") write_h5ad(adata, path) roundtrip <- read_h5ad(path) roundtrip #> AnnData object with n_obs × n_vars = 3 × 4 #>     obs: 'cell_type', 'batch' #>     var: 'highly_variable' #>     uns: 'note' #>     obsm: 'pca' #>     layers: 'counts', None (.X) identical(roundtrip$obs_names, adata$obs_names) #> [1] TRUE

title: Getting started with anndata.claude
text: read_h5ad(backed = "r") keeps X (raw$X) disk reads parts indexed. Everything else read memory. Use backed = "r+" write changes X back file. chunked_X() visits rows X chunks chunk_X() returns random chosen rows. to_memory() loads whole object write_h5ad() copy(filename) write backed object new file. Assigning X ends backed mode, file left unchanged. sparse_dataset() makes handle sparse matrix open rhdf5 group, also $append() add rows columns disk.
code: backed <- read_h5ad(path, backed = "r") backed$isbacked #> [1] TRUE backed$filename #> [1] "/tmp/RtmpDOcvYs/file1da8446d51d9.h5ad" backed$X[1:2, c(1, 3)] #>      [,1] [,2] #> [1,]    1    7 #> [2,]    2    8 chunks <- backed$chunked_X(2) length(chunks) #> [1] 2 chunks[[2]]$start #> [1] 3 backed$chunk_X(I(3)) #>      [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4] #> [1,]    3    6    9   12 in_memory <- backed$to_memory() in_memory$isbacked #> [1] FALSE backed$file$close()

title: Getting started with anndata.claude
text: read_lazy() reads h5ad file zarr store AnnData whose X, layers, mappings, obs var lazy. Arrays DelayedArrays (sparse ones stay sparse) data frame columns read used. uns read memory. Subsetting, Views, copy() t() stay lazy, to_memory() reads everything. Writing lazy object supported yet, call to_memory() first. read_elem_lazy() single Element, chunks sets chunk shape DelayedArray grid.

text: concat() combines AnnData objects along axis ("obs" default) follows Python’s concat(). inner join keeps variables every object outer join keeps , filling new entries fill_value. named list gives keys, label stores obs index_unique adds names. merge uns_merge choose annotations axis uns entries kept ("", "unique", "first" "", function). Views backed objects can concatenated, objects read_lazy() give lazy result.
code: a <- AnnData(   matrix(1, nrow = 2, ncol = 2),   obs = data.frame(row.names = c("a1", "a2")),   var = data.frame(row.names = c("g1", "g2")) ) b <- AnnData(   matrix(2, nrow = 2, ncol = 2),   obs = data.frame(row.names = c("b1", "b2")),   var = data.frame(row.names = c("g2", "g3")) ) concat(list(a, b))$var_names #> [1] "g2" concat(list(a, b), join = "outer")$X #>      [,1] [,2] [,3] #> [1,]    1    1   NA #> [2,]    1    1   NA #> [3,]   NA    2    2 #> [4,]   NA    2    2 combined <- concat(   list(first = a, second = b),   label = "batch",   index_unique = "-" ) combined$obs #> DataFrame with 4 rows and 1 column #>              batch #>           <factor> #> a1-first    first  #> a2-first    first  #> b1-second   second #> b2-second   second

title: Differences from Python anndata
text: R indices. Indices 1-based, negative integers exclude, logical vectors need full axis length character vectors match names (first match). Zero, NA, unknown names mixed signs raise anndata_index_error. Reason: R semantics (roadmap principles, core-object spec “Subsetting”). Help page: ?anndata-index. Mapping keys. Keys obsm, varm, obsp, varp, layers uns must single non-empty strings, R lists hold NA empty names. Python accepts key (core-object/05). Data frames obsp varp. data frame error. Python converts homogeneous one array, spec allows matrices (core-object/05). Non-character obs_names list. list obs non-character names coerced character anndata_implicit_modification_warning. Python keeps (core-object/02). Assigning obs var. value without names resets names "0", "1", … Python, obs_names<- accepts duplicates without warning (Python warns construction), see core-object/07. raw$X raw$var can assigned. R keeps validated setters adata$raw$var$col <- v works, Python modifies place (core-object/08).

title: Differences from Python anndata
text: Help page: ?AnnData Accessors return plain R values. Python x = view.X; x[0, 0] = 1 modifies View, R x <- view$X; x[1, 1] <- 1 changes x. Assign View (view$X[1, 1] <- 1) instead. Reason: R values copied modification (ADR 0002 views spec). Warnings broader. R tell view$obs$col <- x view$obs <- x, setting obs, var, uns X always makes View actual warning, Python silent forms (views/03). item assignment X, layers obsm says “Setting element” Python says “Trying modify attribute”. Nested values snapshots. change nested value uns never reaches parent, view$obs$num[1] <- v detaches instead raising pandas’ ChainedAssignmentError (views/02 views/03). View backed object. view$X[1, 1] <- 5 makes View actual warning, Python silently changes nothing (backed/05).

Moving backed View’s file fails anything moved (anndata_file_not_found_error move fails), Python renames file first leaves corrupt. Writing existing file. Writing new path exists truncates , Python opens append mode updates (backed/05). Backed raw (backed/05). Writing backed raw place raises anndata_not_supported_error (Python fails AttributeError), writing new file works. filename <- NULL keeps values raw$X, Python leaves None. raw$X<- exists R nested assignment refused backed raw. chunked_X() generator. returns list list(chunk, start, end) 1-based inclusive rows, generator 0-based half-open ranges (backed/06).

title: Differences from Python anndata

Lazy frames indexed row name. Python’s Dataset2D loc (lazy/07). read_elem_lazy() takes path handle. R element object like h5py’s (lazy/07). int32 array holding -2^31. NA_integer_ bit pattern, lazy seed (whose type fixed reading) raises anndata_dtype_overflow_error block realised, suggests eager read (lazy/04). R types. Lazy arrays DelayedArray’s R types promoted -disk dtype (concat/06).

Annotation columns Python turn mixed object column (numbers strings, bool numbers) raise anndata_unsupported_value_error. Keys converted character (concat/03).

title: Differences from Python anndata
text: NA NaN. Double NA_real_ NaN written NaN, read back NaN (h5ad-io spec, “Encodings”). --range sparse indices. Help page: ?h5ad. CSR CSC matrix whose indices range shape (1-based indices Illumina DRAGEN 4.5.4 writes) raises anndata_io_registry_error, hint look 1-based. Python reads file without complaint invalid scipy matrix (check_format() fails toarray() misplaces values), Matrix hold invalid matrix. Unsorted sparse indices. Unsorted indices CSR CSC matrix sorted read, data, Matrix needs sorted. matrix -disk order indices data can differ (ADR 0006). Compression rec-arrays. Help page: ?io-rec-array. compression = "lzf" writes HDF5 rec-array uncompressed, compound helper supports gzip (ADR 0008 h5ad-io/15). zarr rec-array chunks. zarr rec-array written one chunk, Python uses zarr’s guess_chunks (zarr-io/14). complex64. Reading complex64 raises classed error naming path, rhdf5 read (h5ad-io spec, “Encodings”). See also vignette("anndata-claude") overview.
